One acceptance boundary I’d keep explicit for `session.next.*`: before a resumed/tailed Session is allowed to run the next model/tool step, expose a small resume receipt, not just a replay cursor.

For this PR’s shape that could be: Location/session id, admitted `session_input` id, current `EventV2.Cursor`, projection version or last durable event applied, whether a process-local wake was only advisory vs promoted from the inbox, pending local tool calls with approval state carried/expired, and whether provider continuation metadata was restored or intentionally reset.

That gives HTTP/SDK consumers a testable invariant: replay may rebuild history from SQLite, but execution only continues after the runtime can show which durable boundary it is trusting and what must be revalidated before side effects.

This is distinct from the three issues mentioned:

- **#29734** — about adding fallback/logging when title generation fails; doesn't address the opencode provider config gap
- **#20269** — about `effort`/variant parameters leaking into the small model call (affects Anthropic/etc.); root cause is in how `user.variant` is passed through, not in `smallOptions`

This issue (#30662) is specifically about `smallOptions()` in `transform.ts` lacking opencode provider handling. The `options()` function sets `promptCacheKey`, `include` (`INCLUDE_ENCRYPTED_REASONING`), and `reasoningSummary` for opencode models, but `smallOptions()` returns an empty `{}`. This is a separate, concrete code gap that affects all opencode provider models regardless of variants or model resolution.

All four are valid bugs that compound — fixing all four would give robust title generation.

Thanks. This is related to #16882, but I intentionally kept this separate because I verified the behavior still exists on `1.15.13` and the repro adds a more specific current failure mode.

Additional details now added to the issue body:

- The session had already been manually compacted (`auto:false`) before the later automatic compactions.
- Two automatic compactions were then created consecutively with `auto:true, overflow:true` despite `compaction.auto:false`.
- The first automatic compaction happened when the last successful request was only `154,038 / 568,000 = 27.1%` of the configured context window for `github-copilot/gpt-5.5`.
- The second automatic compaction happened immediately after that; the compaction summary request itself was only `22,365 / 568,000 = 3.9%` of context.
- The likely trigger was not normal token-threshold overflow, but provider/media/request-payload overflow after reading image attachments, including one attachment JSON payload around `1.78 MB`.

So this confirms the issue is not just proactive auto-compaction ignoring the setting. The provider/processor `result === "compact"` recovery path appears to bypass `compaction.auto:false` and hardcodes `auto:true`, even when the overflow is caused by media/request payload rather than context window usage.

I reproduced this on Windows with OpenCode 1.15.13: normal `opencode run` worked, while starting the TUI failed during OpenTUI renderer startup with error 126 from a virtual Bun path like `B:/~BUN/root/opentui-*.dll`.

I opened a draft fix in #30673. The PR does not just improve the error message; it ships `opentui.dll` as a real Windows sidecar next to `opencode.exe`, copies it during postinstall, and calls OpenTUI's `setRenderLibPath()` before renderer creation.

Local validation for the PR:
- `bun --cwd packages/opencode test --timeout 30000 test/cli/opentui-native.test.ts` passed.
- `bun --cwd packages/opencode script/build.ts --single --skip-install --skip-embed-web-ui` passed and produced `dist/opencode-windows-x64/bin/opentui.dll`.
- A built Windows TUI smoke test rendered without the local `B:` workaround and did not hit error 126.

Full workspace `bun --cwd packages/opencode typecheck` still failed in my local checkout due to unrelated current `dev` workspace/module errors outside this PR, so I left the PR as draft with that limitation called out.

I investigated this and prepared a fix.

Root cause appears to be stale project-root resolution in `layout.tsx`:

- `projectRoot(directory)` can return a root from `serverSync.data.project` based on persisted project metadata.
- After moving/renaming folders (for example OneDrive path -> local path), that metadata can still point to an old worktree path.
- Navigation then reuses the stale root and keeps restoring/reading session-route state under the old location.

Fix approach:

- In `projectRoot(directory)`, only trust metadata-derived roots when they still match a currently known open project root.
- If metadata resolves to a stale/non-open root, fall back to the currently selected directory.

This prevents stale path restoration from hijacking navigation after folder moves.

I investigated this path and prepared a fix.

Root cause: cache token extraction in `Session.getUsage()` was mostly usage-field driven (`usage.cacheReadInputTokens` / `usage.cacheWriteInputTokens`) with provider-specific metadata fallback for Anthropic/Vertex/Bedrock/Venice only.

For custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, cache counts can arrive in provider metadata under an OpenAI-style payload (`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`) instead of normalized usage fields. In that case, session token accounting records cache read/write as zero, which matches the symptom reported for exported subagent sessions.

Fix approach:

- Add metadata fallback parsing in `Session.getUsage()` for OpenAI-style metadata usage payloads.
- Extract `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` as cache read fallback.
- Keep existing provider-specific write-token fallbacks and add generic metadata write fallbacks (`cache_creation_input_tokens` / `cacheWriteInputTokens`).

- keep `undefined` for empty descriptions

I also added a regression test with `description: |` multiline YAML in `packages/opencode/test/skill/skill.test.ts` to verify the description is loaded as expected.

I investigated this and prepared a fix.

Root cause
- In `SessionPrompt.resolvePart` (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`), non-text/non-directory file attachments (images/binary) were converted directly to data URLs and appended to parts.
- That code path bypassed the Read tool execution flow, so `tool.execute.before` (and `tool.execute.after`) were never triggered.

Fix
- In the image/binary branch, trigger plugin hooks explicitly with Read-equivalent input:
  - `tool.execute.before` with `{ filePath }`
  - perform file read
  - `tool.execute.after` with a minimal Read-style output payload (`Binary read successfully`)
- Keep existing behavior (still attach file as data URL), but now hook-based plugins can inspect/block these reads consistently.
- Preserve error observability in this branch (`log.error` + `Session.Event.Error`) to match neighboring read paths.

Regression test
- Added test in `packages/opencode/test/session/prompt.test.ts`:
  - `fires tool.execute.before for image file parts`
  - Uses a local plugin fixture and verifies both `tool.execute.before` and `tool.execute.after` are called for image file read with expected args.

Additional repro on macOS Desktop 1.15.13.

Scenario:
- Same remote Git repository exists in multiple local directories, each checked out to a different branch and with different working tree state.
- Example shape:
  - `/Users/<user>/Desktop/repo-A` on branch A
  - `/Users/<user>/Desktop/repo-B` on branch B
  - `/Users/<user>/Desktop/repo-C` on branch C
- These are intentionally separate local directories, not intended to be treated as the same active workspace.

Steps observed:
1. Open `repo-A` in OpenCode Desktop.
2. Use the left sidebar `+` to add/open `repo-B`, or use `File -> Open Project` and select `repo-B`.
3. Desktop still shows/activates `repo-A`.
4. Remove `repo-A` from the project list, then try opening `repo-B` again.
5. Desktop still comes back to `repo-A`.

Expected:
- OpenCode Desktop should distinguish projects by the selected local directory path, or at least allow multiple local clones/worktrees of the same remote repo to appear as separate workspaces.
- Selecting `repo-B` should switch the session root/workspace to `repo-B`, not the first opened clone.

Actual:
- Desktop appears to merge these directories by repository identity/remote and keeps resolving back to the first recorded directory.
- This makes parallel branch development with multiple local directories unusable because the UI cannot reliably switch to the intended working tree.

Local state evidence:
- `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/opencode.global.dat` stores `server.projects.local` with `worktree` entries and `lastProject.local` still pointing at the first opened directory.
- Clearing recent desktop state did not fix the behavior; reopening another clone of the same repo still resolves back to the first directory.

This is not just session history sharing. The active project/workspace path itself is wrong, so edits/reviews can target the wrong checkout.

In macOS

opencode run shows:

 - SQLITE_READONLY on ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
 - EACCES creating lock files in ~/.local/state/opencode/locks/...

Run this once to fix ownership:

```
 sudo chown -R "$USER":"$(id -gn)" \
   ~/.local/state/opencode \
   ~/.local/share/opencode \
   ~/.config/opencode

```
Then restart opencode normally (without sudo):

 opencode

If it still fails, remove stale DB/lock files and retry:

 rm -f ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db{,-wal,-shm}
 rm -rf ~/.local/state/opencode/locks
 opencode

This migration breaks upgraded beta DBs with pre-durable session projections. On an affected DB: 2,040 session_message rows total, 1,993 have no matching event.id across 237 sessions, 47 match across 1 session, and 0 sessions mix matched/unmatched rows. These are historical projections rather than partial corruption, but 20260603040000_session_message_projection_order rejects them with: Cannot migrate session_message projections without matching durable events. Suggested fix: backfill durable rows from event.seq; for legacy-only sessions assign seq using the prior deterministic (time_created, id) order; keep rejecting mixed sessions. Desktop currently surfaces this as an indefinite loading animation because the sidecar exits before readiness.
